conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: BLOCK CONTAINS clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: Printed format: BLOCK [CONTAINS] [integer-1 TO] integer-2 {[CHARACTERS] | RECORDS} (BLOCK/TO/RECORDS underlined; CONTAINS and CHARACTERS optional words, so omitting the unit word = CHARACTERS). Grammar: BLOCK CONTAINS? integerLiteral (TO integerLiteral)? (CHARACTERS | RECORDS)? - exact. Placement: fileDescriptionClause alternative (FD only; SD excluded per sortMergeDescriptionEntry). Probed pinned cobol.exe at --std 85 and 2023: 'BLOCK CONTAINS 2 RECORDS', 'BLOCK 100', 'BLOCK CONTAINS 10 TO 100 CHARACTERS', 'BLOCK CONTAINS 10 TO 20' all compile and run; '+5' and '5.5' refused (COBOL0001, integer-n required); 'CHARACTERS RECORDS' refused (COBOL0307, braces choose one); zero refused COBOLNET2386 (§5.5 1) nonzero default). conformance:2023/pb829_closed_formats_legal exercises only the 'BLOCK CONTAINS 1 RECORDS' arm, so it is not a covering test for the whole format -> test-ref empty. cite.py --check 13.18.10.1 "The BLOCK CONTAINS clause specifies the size of a physical record." -> OK. || Editions (adjudicator): 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (clause present unchanged in every edition; Annex E records no change to 13.18.10)
rows.rule-text:
╭ CHARACTERS ╮ BLOCK CONTAINS [ integer-1 TO ] integer-2 ┤ ├ ╰ RECORDS ╯
> **Figure notes (BLOCK CONTAINS clause syntax diagram).** `BLOCK`, `TO`, and `RECORDS` are underlined in the printed standard (required words). `CONTAINS` and `CHARACTERS` are **not** underlined — they are optional words. The braces select exactly one of `CHARACTERS` / `RECORDS`; the `integer-1 TO` phrase is optional.

rows.subject: BLOCK CONTAINS clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 13.18.10.4 "This clause is required except when one or more of the following conditions exist" -> OK GR1. The managed I-O model writes one logical record per physical record (no blocking), so condition a) always holds and the clause is never required; accepting FDs without it (every corpus program) is conforming, and there is no case where omission must be diagnosed. docs/CONFORMANCE.md A.3 row 5 = Claimed (inert): 'Accepted; no effect on the managed I-O model'. cite.py --check A.3 "The BLOCK CONTAINS clause has no effect if the operating environment does not support the required features" -> OK §A.3 5). No binder/emitter/runtime site reads blockContainsClause (grep of src: only CobolData.g4 and IntegerOperandPass.Slots reference it); the managed I-O model does no blocking. || Editions (adjudicator): 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (clause present unchanged in every edition; Annex E records no change to 13.18.10)
rows.rule-text: This clause is required except when one or more of the following conditions exist: a) A physical record contains one and only one complete logical record. b) The hardware device assigned to the file has one and only one physical record size. c) The number of records or characters contained in a block is specified in the operating environment.

rows.subject: BLOCK CONTAINS clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 13.18.10.4 "in which case the RECORDS phrase shall not be used" -> OK GR2. The three situations (records spanning physical records in mass storage, padding in the physical record, grouping implying an inaccurate size) describe the implementation's physical layout; with no blocking none arises, so RECORDS is always usable and accepting it (probe 'BLOCK CONTAINS 2 RECORDS' at 85/2023 compiles and runs) is correct. docs/CONFORMANCE.md A.3 row 5 = Claimed (inert): 'Accepted; no effect on the managed I-O model'. cite.py --check A.3 "The BLOCK CONTAINS clause has no effect if the operating environment does not support the required features" -> OK §A.3 5). No binder/emitter/runtime site reads blockContainsClause (grep of src: only CobolData.g4 and IntegerOperandPass.Slots reference it); the managed I-O model does no blocking. || Editions (adjudicator): 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (clause present unchanged in every edition; Annex E records no change to 13.18.10)
rows.rule-text: The size of a physical record may be stated in terms of records unless one or more of the following situations exists, in which case the RECORDS phrase shall not be used: a) In mass storage files, logical records may extend across physical records. b) The physical record contains padding (area not contained in a logical record). c) Logical records are grouped in such a manner that an inaccurate physical record size would be implied.

rows.subject: BLOCK CONTAINS clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 13.18.10.4 "regardless of the types of characters used to represent the items within the physical record" -> OK GR3. Defines the unit of a CHARACTERS size (bytes). The physical-record size has no effect in this implementation, which A.3 item 5 sanctions and CONFORMANCE.md documents (§4.2.6 documentation duty met by row 5). Nothing observable to diverge. docs/CONFORMANCE.md A.3 row 5 = Claimed (inert): 'Accepted; no effect on the managed I-O model'. cite.py --check A.3 "The BLOCK CONTAINS clause has no effect if the operating environment does not support the required features" -> OK §A.3 5). No binder/emitter/runtime site reads blockContainsClause (grep of src: only CobolData.g4 and IntegerOperandPass.Slots reference it); the managed I-O model does no blocking. || Editions (adjudicator): 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (clause present unchanged in every edition; Annex E records no change to 13.18.10)
rows.rule-text: If the CHARACTERS phrase is specified, the physical record size is specified in terms of the number of bytes required to store the physical record, regardless of the types of characters used to represent the items within the physical record.

rows.subject: BLOCK CONTAINS clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 13.18.10.4 "If integer-1 is not specified, integer-2 represents the exact size of the physical record." -> OK GR4. Exact vs min/max physical record size has no runtime effect under the documented inert claim (A.3 item 5). The one compile-time consequence of the min/max reading - their ordering - is SR1 (DIVERGES, separate row); §13.4.5.4 GR2a's EXTERNAL agreement on min/max is a different rule, not adjudicated here. docs/CONFORMANCE.md A.3 row 5 = Claimed (inert): 'Accepted; no effect on the managed I-O model'. cite.py --check A.3 "The BLOCK CONTAINS clause has no effect if the operating environment does not support the required features" -> OK §A.3 5). No binder/emitter/runtime site reads blockContainsClause (grep of src: only CobolData.g4 and IntegerOperandPass.Slots reference it); the managed I-O model does no blocking. || Editions (adjudicator): 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (clause present unchanged in every edition; Annex E records no change to 13.18.10)
rows.rule-text: If integer-1 is not specified, integer-2 represents the exact size of the physical record. If integer-1 and integer-2 are both specified, they refer to the minimum and maximum size of the physical record, respectively.

rows.subject: Boolean literals
rows.adjudicator-notes: Format 1 B"[0|1]..."/B'...' and Format 2 BX"[hex]..."/BX'...' with the character sequence OPTIONAL under both delimiters. BOOL_BODY = 'B' '"' [01]* '"' | 'B' apostrophe [01]* apostrophe | 'BX' '"' HEXDIGITS '"' | 'BX' apostrophe HEXDIGITS apostrophe, HEXDIGITS=[0-9a-f]* (caseInsensitive lexer). Probes out/probe/boolean-literals/bl1 (B"0101", B'10', BX"...", BX'f0', VALUE BX'0f') and bl12 (B"", B'', BX'', BX"") all accepted with correct values. cite.py --check 8.3.3.4.2 "hexadecimal-boolean" OK. No spec-derived test exercises the apostrophe spelling of either format (r03 covers BX"..." only) -> test-ref empty. Doc drift (not a verdict issue): CobolLexer.g4 comments above BOOLLIT and near line 979 still say 'BX"..." (hex boolean) is deferred', and the HEXDIGITS comment says Format 1 is '[01]+' while the rule is [01]*. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2002, 2014, 2023 (boolean literals are a COBOL-2002 introduction, gated COBOLNET0900 at --std 85 - probe bl7; the zero-length-literal introduction edge is not derivable from the in-repo 2023 text, whose Annex E lists only the 2014->2023 delta)
rows.rule-text:
Format 1 (boolean) 
 ╭ B"[boolean-character-1] … " ╮ ┤ ├ ╰ B'[boolean-character-1] … ' ╯
Format 2 (hexadecimal-boolean) 
 ╭ BX"[hexadecimal-digit-1] … " ╮ ┤ ├ ╰ BX'[hexadecimal-digit-1] … ' ╯

rows.subject: CALL statement (calling a non-COBOL program)
rows.adjudicator-notes: Verified by reading ProgramTable.ProbeSiblingModule (loads <name>.dll from AppContext.BaseDirectory, exact then case-insensitive; no __CobolModule.Register -> false; any load exception -> false) and by probes: /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s1/probe/i16t.cob (>>TURN EC-PROGRAM CHECKING ON, --std 2002/2023): CALL "Antlr4.Runtime.Standard" (a real foreign .NET dll beside the compiler), CALL identifier 'System.Runtime', CALL "Cobol.Net.Runtime" all take ON EXCEPTION with EXCEPTION-STATUS EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND; i16o.cob --std 85 ON OVERFLOW taken, --std 2023 ON EXCEPTION taken / NOT ON EXCEPTION not; i16n.cob without ON EXCEPTION -> abnormal run-unit termination naming EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND. cite.py --check 14.9.4.4 'If the called program is a COBOL program, its execution is described in 14.2, Procedure division structure; otherwise the execution is defined by the implementor' OK (3g). No spec-derived witness exists (a conformance-test deploying a foreign dll beside the program would pin it) — row says —. The adjacent located-but-unloadable edge (reported as NOT-FOUND instead of RESOURCES) is kb/Work PB1422 (item 14), not stated here. Owning note: A11.
rows.rule-text: CALL statement (calling a non-COBOL program). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (14.9.4, CALL statement, General rule 3g)

rows.subject: CALL-CONVENTION directive
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: "The default for the CALL-CONVENTION directive is '>>CALL-CONVENTION COBOL'." (cite.py: OK §7.3.9.3 1)). The compiler holds no call-convention state (DirectiveStateRegistry row: 'every name is processed under the §7.3.9.3 GR1 default (COBOL)'), so with no directive every CALL/CANCEL/program-address/INVOKE name is processed under the COBOL mapping. Probe probe/callconv/A.cob (no directive): CALL "ccsubA" and CALL "CCSUBA" both reach PROGRAM-ID CCSUBA -> 'IN SUB' twice at 2023; same at --std 2002 (B.cob). The explicit '>>CALL-CONVENTION COBOL' (B.cob) is indistinguishable, as GR1 requires. --std 85 rejects the directive with COBOLNET0900 (facility introduced 2002). No spec-derived test asserts the default mapping (tests/conformance/2002/pb725_directive_facility.cob only proves the directive compiles and says 'no call convention varies here'), so test-ref empty. || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the §7.3 directive facility; absent in COBOL-85)
rows.rule-text: The default for the CALL-CONVENTION directive is '>>CALL-CONVENTION COBOL'.

rows.subject: CALL-CONVENTION directive
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'The CALL-CONVENTION directive may also be used by the implementor to determine other details needed to interact with a function, method, or program.' (cite.py OK §7.3.9.3 3)). Permissive ('may'): it grants the implementor latitude and imposes no obligation. COBOL.NET uses no call-convention to select linkage details (single .NET managed calling convention, docs/CONFORMANCE.md recognized-and-ignored directives entry; DirectiveStateRegistry 'NONE HELD'). Declining an optional latitude conforms. Nothing observable to test.
rows.rule-text: The CALL-CONVENTION directive may also be used by the implementor to determine other details needed to interact with a function, method, or program.

rows.subject: CHAR function (which one of the multiple characters is returned)
rows.adjudicator-notes: Verified by reading LocaleCollation.CharAt (returns OrderVector.FirstOfRank[position], the lowest code unit collating at that rank; field comment cites §15.15.4 r2) and by probes: /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s1/probe/i21.cob (PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS LOC, ALPHABET LOC IS LOCALE; --std 2002 and 2023): ORD(X"00")=ORD(X"01")=ORD(X"1F")=1, CHAR(1) -> CONVERT(..ANY ANUM HEX)=00, stable across two invocations; i21b.cob (ALPHABET AL IS "C" ALSO "A" ALSO "B" "D"; --std 85 and 2023): ORD("A")=1, CHAR(1)=C (branch 1, standard-defined; pinned separately by conformance:2002/pb59_char_representative, which does not pin this determination). No alphanumeric twin of l1_char_national_locale_tie exists, so Pinned-by is —. cite.py --check 15.15.4 'If the order of multiple characters having the same position is undefined, the implementor shall define which of those multiple characters is returned' OK (2); 12.3.7.4 'Literal-1 is the first character in the sequence ...' OK. Owning note: A11.
rows.rule-text: CHAR function (which one of the multiple characters is returned). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (15.15, CHAR function, Returned value, rule 2)

rows.subject: CLASS-ID paragraph
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'Object-class-name-2 shall not inherit from object-class-name-1 directly or indirectly.' (cite.py --check 11.3.3 -> OK §11.3.3 4)). Probe out/probe/class-id-paragraph/cycle.cob CYA INHERITS CYB, CYB INHERITS CYA (each in the other's REPOSITORY) -> COBOLNET0820 at (2,18) 'the INHERITS chain is cyclic through CYA (ISO §11.3.2 ...)'. The walk is transitive (HashSet over the Base chain) so an n-cycle is caught, and the link is cut so downstream walks terminate. One diagnostic per cycle (acceptable; the source is rejected). Single inheritance only, so the chain walk covers every path (multi-base refused 0849). Citation is §11.3.2 rather than §11.3.3 SR4 (finding inherits-cycle-citation). No covering test found.
rows.rule-text: Object-class-name-2 shall not inherit from object-class-name-1 directly or indirectly.

rows.subject: COBOL character repertoire
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'When an implementation does not provide a graphic representation of all characters of the COBOL character repertoire, substitute graphics may be specified by the implementor to replace the characters not represented.' (cite.py --check 8.1.3.2 -> OK 8.1.3.2 5)). A permission conditioned on a missing graphic. The source is decoded to UTF-16, which represents every Table 1 basic letter, digit and special character (all in ISO/IEC 646 IRV) and every Annex B character, so the antecedent is false and no substitute graphic is used or needed -- verified by reading ReadAllText and by the probes (rcase/rcase2 exercise the basic set incl. hyphen, quote, parentheses, period). No latitude exercised. Documenting 'substitute graphics: none' belongs to A.1 item 25 = DOC-A.1-25, the same missing CONFORMANCE.md row noted on GR-8.1.3.2-1; it does not make this permissive rule defective. CONFORMS-but-untested. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (no Annex E change)
rows.rule-text: When an implementation does not provide a graphic representation of all characters of the COBOL character repertoire, substitute graphics may be specified by the implementor to replace the characters not represented.
